content_of_post_to_comment: Question for my metric-using friends: In American English, we have a phrase “your mileage may vary.” Basically what works for me might not work for you. But metric doesn’t use miles. Is there an equivalent saying using kilometers? Or another idiom that captures the same concept without using the units of measure? Asking for an ignorant American
comment: Interesting that the idiom survives because “mileage” became a metaphor, not a measurement. Maybe the metric equivalent isn’t a unit swap but a shift from distance to context: results may vary.
